extracted.intended_audience: general readers, researchers, and journalists interested in QAnon and online content moderation
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia article summarizing the QAnon conspiracy movement, named actors, and platform responses (content removals, bans, policy changes) across major social networks and app stores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reddit ban criteria: encouraging/inciting violence & posting personal/confidential information
rubrics_metrics.description: Reddit banned the community /r/CBTS_Stream for "encouraging or inciting violence and posting personal and confidential information."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grounds for community removal include content that encourages or incites violence and the dissemination of personal/confidential information; example: followers moved to Discord after bans. (Page reference: March 2018 ban of /r/CBTS_Stream.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinated inauthentic behavior (Facebook removals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Facebook removed pages, accounts, and groups linked to "individuals associated with the QAnon network" as part of an investigation into "suspected coordinated inauthentic behavior."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platforms may remove networks rather than only individual posts when they identify coordinated inauthentic campaigns spreading conspiracies or misinformation (example: May 2020 Facebook takedown).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dangerous Individuals and Organizations policy (Facebook expansion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Facebook expanded its Dangerous Individuals and Organizations policy to address "growing movements that, while not directly organizing violence, have celebrated violent acts, shown that they have weapons and suggest they will use them, or have individual followers with patterns of violent behavior."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under this policy expansion platforms may remove groups/pages even if they do not explicitly organize violence, if they celebrate violent acts, display weapons, suggest intent, or have followers with violent patterns; Facebook reported large-scale removals and hashtag/feature restrictions following this change (Aug 19, 2020).

rubrics_metrics.name: Blanket representation bans (Facebook October 2020 rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Facebook announced it would "immediately begin removing any Facebook Pages, Groups and Instagram accounts representing QAnon, even if they contain no violent content."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a movement is designated disallowed, representation alone (affiliation/branding) can be sufficient for removal — platforms may remove accounts/groups regardless of specific violent content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Twitter enforcement: coordinated amplification & offline-harm potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Twitter banned more than 7,000 accounts connected to QAnon for coordinated amplification of fake news and conspiracy theories, stating enforcement applies to behavior "that has the potential to lead to offline harm."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria include coordinated amplification of misinformation/conspiracies and any platform behavior judged likely to cause offline harm; Twitter indicated actions could scale to many accounts (July 2020 and post-Jan 6, 2021 responses).

rubrics_metrics.name: YouTube policy: banning conspiracy content used to justify real-world violence
rubrics_metrics.description: YouTube modified its hate and harassment policies to bar "content that targets an individual or group with conspiracy theories that have been used to justify real-world violence," while allowing non-targeting discussion of QAnon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platform distinguishes between general discussion of a conspiracy (permitted) and content that targets individuals/groups with conspiratorial claims that have historically justified violence (prohibited); YouTube reported reduced recommendations for QAnon content and policy updates to curb targeted conspiracies.

rubrics_metrics.name: App store terms-of-service enforcement (Google/Apple removals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Google removed apps (QMAP, Q Alerts!, Q Alerts LITE) from Google Play for violating its terms of service; Apple pulled the QDrops app after media inquiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: App stores can remove apps that promote conspiracy theories or otherwise breach store policies; popularity metrics (e.g., QDrops being a top paid app) do not prevent removal if terms are violated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marketplace and retailer removals (Etsy, Amazon)
rubrics_metrics.description: Etsy announced it would remove all QAnon-related merchandise; Amazon removed a pro-QAnon book after the Capitol riots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E-commerce platforms may remove products/content tied to disallowed movements or which are linked to real-world harm or policy violations; enforcement timing can be reactive to events (e.g., post-riot removals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Infrastructure take-down risk for extremist content (hosting/hosting-providers actions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parler was taken offline by Amazon Web Services after significant QAnon and far-right extremist content following the Capitol attack.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond social networks, infrastructure providers (hosting, cloud services) may deplatform services that host large amounts of extremist or violent content, resulting in temporary or prolonged outages of platforms popular with such movements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mass-suspension response tied to real-world events
rubrics_metrics.description: Following the January 6, 2021 Capitol attack, platforms (Twitter, Facebook) suspended tens of thousands of QAnon-focused accounts and removed "Stop the Steal" content in coordinated actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platforms may enact large-scale suspensions in response to acute events linking online activity to offline violence; such actions are often claimed to prevent further harm and reduce immediate mobilization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nuanced allowance: permitting non-targeting discussion of conspiracies
rubrics_metrics.description: YouTube (and other platforms) indicated they would still allow content discussing QAnon if it did not target individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy nuance: educational, journalistic, or critical discussion of a conspiracy theory may be allowed provided it does not propagate targeted conspiratorial allegations about identifiable individuals or groups linked to violence.
